properties.biography: Born in Manhattan in 1977, Fiona Apple showed musical talent early and began playing piano and writing songs as a teenager. She was discovered in the mid-1990s and released her debut album Tidal (1996), which featured the breakthrough single "Criminal" and earned widespread acclaim. Over subsequent albums — including When the Pawn..., Extraordinary Machine, The Idler Wheel..., and Fetch the Bolt Cutters — she evolved from lushly arranged, producer-driven recordings to increasingly idiosyncratic, rhythmically adventurous and self-assertive works. Known for meticulous songwriting and a fiercely personal voice, Apple has maintained a selective public profile while influencing generations of singer-songwriters.
properties.known_for: Emotive, confessional songwriting; piano-driven compositions; distinctive, expressive voice; uncompromising artistic vision and critically acclaimed albums.
properties.description: Fiona Apple is an American singer-songwriter and pianist whose work blends confessional lyricism, complex piano arrangements, and bold rhythmic choices. Emerging in the mid-1990s with widely acclaimed songwriting and the hit single "Criminal," she has built a reputation for emotionally raw performances, inventive production, and albums that defy easy pop categorization. Her records combine alternative rock, jazz-tinged harmonies, and art-pop sensibilities, earning consistent critical praise and a devoted international audience.

They released their debut and only album, 'Mary Star of the Sea', in 2003, which received critical acclaim for its catchy melodies and energetic performances. Despite the promising start, internal tensions led to the band's breakup later that year.

properties.biography: Born in Duncan in the Cowichan Valley of Vancouver Island, Mac DeMarco emerged in the late 2000s/early 2010s as a distinctive voice in indie music. He began releasing recordings on independent labels and gained wider attention with catalogues issued through Captured Tracks. Across albums like 2 (early breakthrough), Salad Days and This Old Dog, DeMarco developed a signature sound marked by jangly, chorus-drenched guitars, warm tape-like production and conversational, confessional lyrics. A prolific multi-instrumentalist and home-recording practitioner, he tours with a loose, charismatic band and has influenced a generation of bedroom-pop and lo-fi artists.

properties.description: Mac DeMarco is a Canadian singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist noted for his relaxed vocal delivery, DIY home-recording approach, and nostalgic, analog-tinged sound. Rising through early independent releases and breakout record label albums, he blends jangly guitars, warm lo-fi production, and wry lyrical observations into melodic songs that bridge indie rock, slacker-pop and bedroom pop. He is widely recognized for albums such as 2, Salad Days, This Old Dog and Here Comes the Cowboy, and for a stage persona that mixes casual humor with intimate performances.
properties.cultural_impact: Mac DeMarco helped popularize a modern slacker/lo-fi aesthetic that influenced numerous bedroom-pop and indie artists; his DIY recording methods and casual public persona shifted expectations for authenticity and informality in indie rock, creating a stylistic blueprint for artists favoring warm analog textures and conversational songwriting.
